title: Mirrors
full_review:
When, early on in the clunky, contrived horror tale “Mirrors” (Fox/Regency) ex-policeman turned security guard Ben Carson (Kiefer Sutherland) finds that the many looking glasses in the burned-out New York department store where he works – also, inevitably, a former mental hospital – are populated by demons intent on killing him and his loved ones, he does what any sensible person would, and stays on the job.

His sister Angela (Amy Smart), with whom he’s been living since separating from his wife Amy (Paula Patton), is the first victim to fall, induced to commit suicide in a spectacularly unpleasant manner by her own reflection. The evil spirits, who can inhabit any reflective surface, next target Amy, along with the couple’s two children, Michael (Cameron Boyce) and Daisy (Erica Gluck).

 

Apart from that one suicide scene, French-born director Alexandre Aja keeps the violence relatively subdued. But his film grows tedious long before its nearly two-hour running time has expired.

The film contains some graphic violence, brief rear and partial nudity, some rough and crude language, and occasional use of profanity. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is L -- limited adult audience, films whose problematic content many adults would find troubling. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted. Under 17 requires accompanying parent or adult guardian.
